processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Five alloys per alloy system synthesized in one operation using five stepwise-moved Cu molds successively filled from a 4-kg ingot; Al charged through an air lock after each cast.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: 10 × 50 × 130 mm³ blocks hot rolled into 2 ± 0.1 mm thick and ~500 mm long sheets

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: After reheating and water quenching, sheets were cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into 2 × 60 × 55 mm³ segments.
Terminal homogenization step defining the as-homogenized reference state; no subsequent aging.
No subsequent aging; this is the as-homogenized (without aging) reference state.
Scales were removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled, water-quenched and homogenized (as-homogenized) material: fully recrystallized austenite-based microstructure with grain size ~20 µm, some retained Mn microsegregations, and Al-dependent ferrite content.

phases_present.volume_fraction: predominant; ~100 vol.% at 2 wt.% Al, decreasing as Al increases
increases with Al content (2–11 wt.% Al)
minor/possible; less relevant than ferrite to the Al-driven trend
may form during quenching for Al contents > 10 wt.%

precipitates.distribution: May form during quenching when Al content exceeds 10 wt.%.
precipitates.coherency: ordered fcc structure with lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic matrix

phase_interfaces.coherence: ordered fcc structure with lattice mismatch below 3% with respect to austenitic Fe-Mn-C matrix

interfaces.slip_behavior: For low-Al members (SIMPLEX TWIP): dislocation-based strain hardening followed by mechanical twinning. For κ-carbide-containing members: Orowan bypassing of longitudinal κ-carbide rods, expansion of dislocation loops assisted by cross-slip, and minor shearing of κ-carbides.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Increasing Al content raises ferrite content; κ-carbides can form during quenching when Al exceeds 10 wt.%.
interfaces.interface_notes: When κ-carbides are embedded in a ferritic matrix, the lattice mismatch can be as large as -6%, leading to semicoherent interfaces and different precipitate morphologies.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: All plotted values represent averages of three measurements for every material state.

yield_strength.value: increases with Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

ultimate_tensile_strength.value: increases with Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

elongation.value: drops as a function of Al content in the range 2–11 wt.% Al

hardness.value: increases with Al content (minimum ~120–140 HBW near 2 wt.% Al, reaching ~290 HBW at ~10.5 wt.% Al; values shown across aging conditions in Fig. 6a4, not resolved separately for the as-quenched/as-homogenized condition)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: performed on the rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: phase characterization/screening (γ austenite, ε martensite, α ferrite, κ carbide)
characterization_methods.key_findings: increasing ferrite content with Al; ferrite content is more relevant than κ-carbides or ε-martensite for the Al-driven strengthening/embrittlement trend.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1; averages of three measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: mechanical screening (yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation)
characterization_methods.key_findings: YS and UTS increase while elongation drops with Al (2–11 wt.% Al).

no cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in final materials; as-cast samples had coarse dendritic microstructure; hot rolling + water quenching gave fully recrystallized microstructure with ~20 µm grain size and some retained Mn microsegregations.

unmapped_findings: The Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl (wt.%) second alloy class comprises five alloys with Al content varied between 2 and 11 wt.%; individual Al levels within this range are not enumerated in the paper [b0019, b0026, b0109].
For Al contents exceeding 10 wt.%, κ-carbides can form during quenching; this applies to the highest-Al member(s) of the Fe-20Mn-0.4C-xAl family [b0032, b0109].
As-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure before hot rolling [b0021].

Across Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels, mass density falls from roughly 7.15 to 6.4 g/cm³ over about 6–13 wt.% Al, with density reduction up to ~18% (Fig. 1); this is family-level context and is not resolved for this specific sample [figure_001, b0007, b0109].
